method.claimBoundary: Documentary governance readiness mapping against GAAM v0.9.0 normative semantics as retained in v0.9.2. No JAZB certification, GAAM conformance, independent assessment, legal validation or operational assurance claim.

findings.title: Organizational authority provenance versus external legitimacy
findings.observation: JAZB identifies an EDA-controlled sovereign root, a human-established Law hierarchy and internal authorization boundaries. The referenced architecture does not establish external recognition of the organization's entitlement to impose a given consequential decision. Source: Phase I §§9, Phase VII Law hierarchy and EDA authority.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Verify the named control boundary in a defined JAZB deployment before asserting implementation or GAAM conformance.

establishes: Internal source and bounded derivation of organizational authority
doesNotEstablish: External legal validity, consent, rights compliance or legitimate standing against outsiders

evidenceExpectation: Signed active Law/version, human establishment record, governing mandate, precedence/escalation decision
candidateTests: Present conflicting organizational Law and independently binding legal constraints; require refusal or escalation rather than silently treating organizational signatures as legitimacy.
knownLimitations: Document-level assessment of user-provided JAZB v2.0 publications; no independently observed JAZB implementation.
Source locations are navigation aids, not redistribution of normative source text.
Readiness status does not amount to a GAAM conformance assessment.

findings.title: Parallel Task and Enforcer governance
findings.observation: Commissioner Law bounds Task operations while parallel Commandant Law governs independently protected Enforcer authority. This documents distinct decision roles but does not prove administrative or execution-path independence in a deployment. Source: Phase II §3.15 and Phase VII Internal Jurisdiction/Commandant Law.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Verify the named control boundary in a defined JAZB deployment before asserting implementation or GAAM conformance.

revocation: Task grant and Enforcer authority suspension

establishes: Specified separation of Task authorization and supervised enforcement
doesNotEstablish: Effective independence of an implemented Enforcer or unbypassable controls

evidenceExpectation: Separate principal assignments, policy control records, enforced path topology, independent negative test results
candidateTests: Attempt Task-to-Enforcer impersonation, policy mutation and direct resource bypass; independently observe and reject unauthorized effects.
knownLimitations: Document-level assessment of user-provided JAZB v2.0 publications; no independently observed JAZB implementation.
Source locations are navigation aids, not redistribution of normative source text.
Readiness status does not amount to a GAAM conformance assessment.

findings.title: Delegation, revocation and in-flight effects
findings.observation: JAZB specifies bounded delegation, revocation, standing Law versions and fail-closed lifecycle controls. Published specification alone does not demonstrate timely propagation into in-flight actions or descendant authorization across independently controlled systems. Source: Phase II delegated authority/lifecycle; Phase IV §2.7 and recovery; Phase VII delegation and revocation requirements.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Verify the named control boundary in a defined JAZB deployment before asserting implementation or GAAM conformance.

establishes: Normative intent for scoped and revocable authority
doesNotEstablish: Deployment-specific propagation latency, transaction cancellation or recovery semantics

evidenceExpectation: Delegation lineage, revocation time, active-version checks, resource-side execution receipt and clock assumptions
candidateTests: Revoke parent delegation between approval and resource commit; verify descendant rejection and an attributable receipt for every attempted effect.
knownLimitations: Document-level assessment of user-provided JAZB v2.0 publications; no independently observed JAZB implementation.
Source locations are navigation aids, not redistribution of normative source text.

findings.title: Internal Customs transfer and jurisdiction distinctions
findings.observation: Version 2.0 explicitly registers internal data-domain Ports alongside external organizational Ports and requires source-to-destination transfer authority distinct from operational access authority. This is a documented jurisdictional separation, not a demonstration of complete route coverage. Source: Phase III §§1, Data Authority Map and internal Port boundaries.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Verify the named control boundary in a defined JAZB deployment before asserting implementation or GAAM conformance.

establishes: Separation of operational authorization from transfer jurisdiction
doesNotEstablish: Automatic coverage of all data routes or third-party recognition of internal rules

evidenceExpectation: EDA-approved Data Authority Map, Port registration, transfer policy, denied-route evidence
candidateTests: Try a restricted-to-general transfer through an unregistered or bypass route while business-access permission remains valid; require denial at the effective transfer boundary.
knownLimitations: Document-level assessment of user-provided JAZB v2.0 publications; no independently observed JAZB implementation.

findings.title: Verified effect evidence, assurance and remedy boundary
findings.observation: JAZB distinguishes approvals and intended change sets from verified receiving-side effects and partial-failure receipts. Such evidence enables reconstruction but does not itself prove authentic observation, independent assurance or affected-party access to challenge and remedy. Source: Phase IV evidence integrity; Phase VI evidence mappings; Phase VII consequential execution and receipts.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Verify the named control boundary in a defined JAZB deployment before asserting implementation or GAAM conformance.

revocation: stop/restrict future effects and preserve prior records

establishes: Proposed chain from authorization to observed effect and evidentiary reconstruction
doesNotEstablish: Truthfulness of all observations, independently validated operations, external appeal or remedy

evidenceExpectation: Approval hash, exact change-set manifest, state preconditions, independently observed resource outcome, audit record and review procedure
candidateTests: Substitute an approved change set, poison observed-effect telemetry, and induce a partial commit; verify independent contradiction detection and accountable review.
knownLimitations: Document-level assessment of user-provided JAZB v2.0 publications; no independently observed JAZB implementation.
Source locations are navigation aids, not redistribution of normative source text.
